subject.title: feat(ui): complete Control UI MCP App bridge

question: Should Control UI accept this consent-gated MCP App capability to submit one plain-text user message through the existing chat-send path?
rationale: Source review can assess the guards, but whether third-party app content should be allowed to initiate a host confirmation and subsequent user-message send is an intentional product security boundary that requires human ownership.

options.title: Approve guarded messaging
options.body: Accept the capability with the current fresh-view authority, exact-text consent, foreground, size, slash-command, rate-limit, and reconstruction-denial controls.

options.title: Keep MCP Apps read-only
options.body: Decline the trust expansion and retain MCP Apps as resource, context, and explicitly authorized tool surfaces without app-initiated chat messages.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded messaging
recommendation.body: Accept the capability with the current fresh-view authority, exact-text consent, foreground, size, slash-command, rate-limit, and reconstruction-denial controls.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the focused implementation history and are the assigned repository member for this MCP Apps bridge work, though approval should be independently reviewed.
